about.title: La Palma Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: La Palma is a small, tightly packed city in Orange County, but that doesn't mean workplace injuries here are any less serious. Warehouse workers, delivery drivers moving through corridors like La Palma Avenue and Orangethorpe Avenue, retail employees, and contractors on local job sites all face real risks on the job. In most cases, California's workers' compensation system is the only path against an employer, regardless of who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the incident, a separate claim against that third party may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect La Palma workers with independent attorneys who can sort through the details of your situation, explain your options, and pursue a claim if one exists, all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why La Palma Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Help You See Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it doesn't account for a negligent third party. We connect you with attorneys who know how to identify when a separate claim may apply.

items.title: Timing Matters, and We Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and a third-party claim carries its own 2-year deadline. Reaching out sooner gives an attorney more room to build your case.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation Is On Your Side
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury. An independent attorney can help make sure your rights are respected while your claim moves forward.

items.question: I already filed a workers' comp claim in La Palma — can I still pursue something else?
items.answer: Yes, in many cases. Workers' compensation and a third-party injury claim aren't mutually exclusive; they address different responsible parties. An independent attorney can review your situation and let you know if a separate claim against a negligent third party makes sense.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Walker Street or La Palma Avenue?
items.answer: If another driver caused the collision while you were working, that driver may be liable separately from any workers' comp benefits you receive. These corridors see a steady volume of reported collisions, and a third-party auto claim could apply depending on the facts.

items.question: Is there a deadline to act on a third-party workplace injury claim?
items.answer: Yes. Third-party claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the injury. Reporting the incident to your employer within 30 days is also important for your workers' comp rights, so it helps to move on both fronts as soon as you're able.
